- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.50) or mixed, model often underestimates downside risk; add buffer for sharp drops or adjust downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day post-spike.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags in adjusting; use sentiment transition as trigger to re-calibrate forecast direction.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: if model is consistently above true price (e.g., >75.5), reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33), model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance or add stochastic adjustment.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to overfitting to recent trends; apply “look-back” rule: if last 5 days are trending, don’t extrapolate beyond 3–5 days unless sentiment confirms.
